speaker: Doctor
text: I see that previous data has suggested a diagnosis, but your symptoms of wrist pain and difficulty in hand movement do not match gastroenteritis. To understand the cause of your injury, please describe exactly how and when this started. REQUEST TEST: Hand_X-Ray.

speaker: Doctor
text: The hand X-ray results are normal, which helps rule out fractures or obvious dislocations. To narrow this down further, have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or weakness specifically in your thumb and index finger?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain radiating from your right thumb and wrist to your elbow, worsening with lifting your infant, is highly suggestive of an elbow pathology rather than just a wrist issue. Did you experience any clicking, locking, or a feeling of instability in your elbow when you were falling six months ago? REQUEST TEST: Elbow_MRI.

speaker: Doctor
text: The Elbow MRI results are currently pending; once we have those, I need to know if you feel any relief or worsening of the pain when you bend your elbow or rotate your forearm. Additionally, does your right thumb deviate inward toward your index finger when you try to extend it against resistance?

speaker: Patient
text: patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of trauma combined with pain radiating to the elbow and worsening with lifting is concerning for a lateral epicondylitis or a radial head injury, but the normal imaging so far requires us to focus on specific functional signs. When you extend your right thumb against resistance, does the pain increase sharply, and do you feel any weakness in that movement?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previous fall on right outstretched hand six months ago. No significant other medical history. Social history: Patient is a mother of an infant, leading a relatively active lifestyle. Does not smoke or consume alcohol regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fall on your outstretched hand six months ago, combined with pain radiating to the elbow that worsens with lifting and improves with ice, is highly suggestive of a specific overuse injury or tendon pathology. To confirm this, have you noticed any swelling or tenderness specifically over the bony prominence on the outer side of your elbow (lateral epicondyle)? REQUEST TEST: Elbow_MRI.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRI results help rule out a significant structural tear or fracture, so we must focus on the clinical signs of tendonitis. When you squeeze a tennis ball or resist me pushing your hand away, does the pain on the outer elbow flare up, and can you grip an object with full strength? REQUEST TEST: Physical_Exam_Lateral_Epicondyle.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Tenderness over the lateral epicondyle with pain on resisted wrist extension and grip testing.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lateral Epicondylitis (Tennis Elbow). The confirmed tenderness over the lateral epicondyle, combined with pain on resisted wrist extension and grip weakness, along with your history of repetitive lifting, is diagnostic for this condition.
